summary: @or-sdk/library-source ships obfuscated preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime to execute an opaque bundled payload
details: On `npm install`, the package's preinstall script `node setup.mjs` downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes it against a shipped 727 KB Bun-compiled bundle `math_init.js` via `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D,'math_init.js')])`. setup.mjs itself is transformed with obfuscator.io-style `_0xNNNNNN` identifier renaming and per-function string-property maps that reconstruct strings such as `/etc/os-release`, `--version`, and `Alpine` at runtime. `math_init.js` is a Bun-serialized CJS blob (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) using a rotated constant array + numeric-index string synthesis decoder (`function WV8StW(a,b,c){for(c=0;c<b;c++)a.push(a.shift());return a}`), shipped without source or documentation. The package presents itself as an SDK type-library, which has no need for a second language runtime or a compiled opaque blob at install time. The combination of an obfuscated install-time script, an alternate-runtime fetch used solely to execute a sibling file (evading Node-level inspection and lifecycle hooks visibility), and an opaque compiled payload is the alternate-runtime-dropper attack pattern: arbitrary attacker-controlled code executes on the installer's host under the installing user's privileges on `npm install`, and its behavior cannot be verified from the shipped source.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
